formation.title: The Kingdom Reborn
formation.text:
The ancient kingdom of Dal Riata, which once bridged the sea between Ireland and Scotland, rises again. From the sacred hilltop of Dunadd where kings once placed their foot upon the inauguration stone, to the holy island of Iona where Columba lit the flame of learning, this land carries memories stretching back to the dawn of the Gaelic world.

The cenela (the great kin-groups who once mustered their galley fleets at the overking's call) look to us now. The Senchus fer nAlban, that ancient census of ships and men, speaks of a people whose power was measured not in fields and castles but in oars and keels. Yet Iona's monks also remind us that Dal Riata's truest legacy was the preservation of civilization itself through the long centuries of darkness.

Shall we be sea-kings, commanding the tides as Aedan mac Gabrain once did? Or shall we be keepers of the sacred flame, as Columba was?

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: Command the seas as our ancestors did

modifiers.name: Sea-Kings' Dominion
modifiers.text: The restored kingdom of Dalriada rules the waves between Ireland and Scotland as its ancestors once did, commanding swift galley fleets through treacherous island waters.

options.text: Rekindle the light of Columba's legacy

modifiers.name: Light of Iona
modifiers.text: Drawing upon the legacy of Columba and the great monastic tradition, the restored Dalriada dedicates itself to scholarship, preservation, and the spread of Gaelic learning across the known world.

advances.name: Seat of Dunadd
advances.text: The restoration of Dunadd as a royal center, where kings place their foot upon the inauguration stone as their ancestors did, symbolizing dominion over the land.

advances.name: Cattle Lords of the West
advances.text: Cattle are the true currency of the Gaelic world. The wealth of a clan chief is measured in the lowing of his herds, and the cattle raid remains the ultimate test of a warrior's boldness. The beasts rendered to the chief are gathered in his folds, and their hides are salted and cured there.

advances.name: The Columban Mission
advances.text: Following the path of St. Columba, who brought the faith from Ireland to Iona in 563, monastic missionaries spread Christianity and literacy throughout the western Highlands and islands.

advances.name: Galley Service of the Cenela
advances.text: The Senchus fer nAlban prescribed naval obligations for each cenela kin-group: two seven-benched galleys for every twenty houses. This galley service made Dalriada a maritime power.

event.title: The Galley Muster
event.text:
The ancient Senchus fer nAlban (the Census of the Men of Scotland) prescribed that every twenty houses owed two seven-benched galleys to the overking's fleet. This system of naval obligation, unique among the kingdoms of Britain, made Dal Riata a maritime power whose reach far exceeded its modest territory.

Now that Dalriada is reborn, the galley muster resumes. From Kintyre to the Outer Hebrides, from the Antrim coast to the islands of Lorne, the cenela prepare their birlinns and long fada for the overking's call. The sea roads that once connected this scattered kingdom are alive with traffic once more.

options.text: Let our enemies tremble at the sight of our sails

modifiers.name: Legacy of Aedan mac Gabrain
modifiers.text: In the spirit of Aedan mac Gabrain, whose fleets ranged from Orkney to the Isle of Man, Dalriada reasserts its command over the western seas.

options.text: Let the monks record what our sailors discover

modifiers.name: Spirit of the Illuminated Page
modifiers.text: The tradition that produced the Book of Kells lives again, as monastic scriptoria produce works of breathtaking artistry and deep learning.

advances.name: Clans Across the Sea
advances.text: The North Channel is no barrier but a highway connecting the Gaelic kindreds of Ireland and Scotland, allowing the free movement of people, ideas, and allegiance.

advances.name: Tanistry Tradition
advances.text: The Gaelic practice of tanistry selects the most capable adult male of the royal kindred as successor, ensuring strong leadership through merit rather than birth order.

advances.name: Island Fortification
advances.text: The scattered islands and sea lochs of western Scotland provide natural defensive positions. With a few men and a fortified promontory, a clan can hold against forces ten times its number.

advances.name: Monastic Scriptorium
advances.text: In the tradition of Iona, monastic scriptoria produce illuminated manuscripts of extraordinary beauty, preserving classical learning while advancing Gaelic literary culture.

advances.name: Herring Fisheries
advances.text: The rich herring runs of the Hebrides and the Minch sustain coastal communities and provide a valuable trade good, salted and exported to markets across northern Europe. Curing yards are raised on the sea lochs.

advances.name: Cenela Muster
advances.text: The formalization of the cenela muster system, where each kin-group provides warriors in proportion to its households, creates a reliable levy that can be assembled quickly by sea.

advances.name: Lordship Customs
advances.text: The overking's authority is reinforced through ancient customs of tribute and feasting, where clan chiefs gather to renew their bonds of obligation and settle disputes.

advances.name: Mainland Diplomacy
advances.text: Dalriada extends its influence beyond the islands through a careful web of marriage alliances, fostering arrangements, and diplomatic treaties with neighboring kingdoms.

advances.name: Galley Warfare
advances.text: The evolution of Dalriadic naval tactics, combining the speed of the birlinn with coastal raiding expertise, produces a fighting style uniquely suited to the island-studded western seaboard.

advances.name: Chartered Markets
advances.text: The establishment of formal market rights at key coastal settlements transforms scattered island trade into a structured commercial network.

advances.name: Highland Grazing Expansion
advances.text: The systematic expansion of sheep and cattle grazing across the Highlands generates wool and livestock for export, though at the cost of displacing some traditional settlements. The townships full and dye the wool in their waulking houses.

advances.name: Clan Justice
advances.text: The codification of brehon law traditions into a formal legal framework, administered by hereditary breitheamh judges, brings order to the realm without destroying its Gaelic character.

event.title: The Breitheamh's Court
event.text:
The ancient Gaelic legal tradition of the brehon (the breitheamh) has been restored under Dalriadic rule. Unlike the feudal courts of England and Scotland, where justice flows downward from the crown, the brehon system is rooted in communal arbitration. The breitheamh sits beneath the open sky, hearing disputes between clansmen, adjudicating cattle claims, and pronouncing judgments according to the Senchus Mor: the great ancient law.

This system of customary justice binds the clans together more effectively than any army. When a man knows his grievances will be heard fairly, he has no cause for rebellion.

advances.name: Gaelic Statecraft
advances.text: Dalriadic diplomats, fluent in the courts of both the Gaelic and English-speaking worlds, prove adept at playing larger powers against each other to preserve the kingdom's independence.

advances.name: Bardic Schools
advances.text:
The formal training of file poets in the classical Gaelic syllabic tradition, requiring up to twelve years of study, produces a scholarly class whose works preserve history and glorify the realm.

Available in: Monastic Scriptorium

advances.name: Armed War Galleys
advances.text: The mounting of cannon aboard the traditional galley hull produces a warship that can navigate the shallow, rocky waters of the Hebrides while delivering devastating broadsides.

advances.name: Highland Levy Reform
advances.text: The reorganization of the clan levy system introduces uniform equipment standards and regular drill, transforming fierce but undisciplined clansmen into reliable soldiers.

advances.name: Cattle Drove Roads
advances.text: The development of formal drove roads allows Highland cattle to be walked to lowland markets in great herds, connecting the pastoral economy to wider commercial networks.

advances.name: Maritime Law of the Isles
advances.text: A codified system of maritime law governs trade, fishing rights, and naval obligations across the island territories, bringing order to the western seaboard.

advances.name: Gaelic Colleges
advances.text: Formal institutions of higher learning, teaching in Gaelic alongside Latin and modern languages, produce a literate administrative class capable of governing a modern state.

advances.name: Clan Regiments
advances.text: The organization of traditional clan warriors into formal regimental structures, retaining their fierce esprit de corps while gaining the discipline of modern warfare.

advances.name: Kelp Industry
advances.text: The harvesting and burning of seaweed along the western coasts produces alkali essential for soap and glass manufacturing, providing a new source of industrial wealth. Kilns are dug along the shore, and glasshouses beside them work with the ash.

advances.name: Gaelic Literary Revival
advances.text:
A conscious effort to collect, preserve, and publish the oral traditions of the Gaelic world produces a literary renaissance, asserting the cultural vitality of the Highland tradition.

Available in: Monastic Scriptorium

event.title: The Gaelic Renaissance
event.text:
A remarkable flowering of Gaelic literature is underway in the restored kingdom. Bardic poets compose elaborate praise-poems in the classical syllabic meters, while monastic scholars copy and annotate ancient texts. The tradition that produced the Book of Kells and the Annals of Ulster is reborn: not as mere imitation, but as a living continuation.

New works in Gaelic are being composed alongside translations from Latin, Greek, and even Arabic, brought by traders along the sea routes. The scriptoria of Dalriada are producing illuminated manuscripts that rival those of any European court.

options.text: Our words will outlast our swords

advances.name: Emigrant Networks
advances.text:
Gaelic emigrants across the Atlantic maintain strong connections to their homeland, creating commercial networks that channel wealth and ideas back to Dalriada.

Available in: Drove Station

advances.name: Modern Fleet
advances.text: The transition from oar-powered galleys to modern sailing vessels, built in the shipyards of the western coast, equips Dalriada with a navy fit for the age of steam.

destiny.name: Destiny of Dalriada
destiny.text: The restored kingdom stands at the crossroads of its fate. The ancient seat of Dunadd beckons, and the cenela await their overking's vision for the realm.

event.title: The Overking's Vision
event.text: From the summit of Dunadd, where the inauguration footprint is carved into the living rock, we survey the realm that is and the realm that might be. The sea roads stretch in every direction: west to the open Atlantic, north to the Norse lands, east to the Scottish mainland, south to Ireland. The question is not whether Dalriada will rise, but how high.

destiny.name: Securing the Northern Isles
destiny.text: To command the western seas, Dalriada must first control the straits and passages that guard the northern approaches. Orkney and the Lothian coast are the keys to this dominion.

conditions.text: Chose the Tides of Dominion destiny

event.title: The Northern Passage Secured
event.text:
The longships of Dalriada now patrol the waters around Orkney, and our banner flies over Edinburgh's rock. The Norse jarls who once raided our coasts with impunity now treat with us as equals. The Pentland Firth (that treacherous strait between Scotland and Orkney) is ours to command.

With the northern approaches secured, the western seaboard lies open before us. No ship passes between the Atlantic and the North Sea without Dalriadic leave.

options.text: The sea roads are ours to command

destiny.name: Command of the Western Seas
destiny.text: With the northern passages secured, Dalriada turns its fleets toward the wider horizon. The Norse ports and the English coast must acknowledge Dalriadic supremacy over the western seas.

event.title: Masters of the Western Sea
event.text:
Dalriadic longships range from Stavanger to York, from the Faroes to the Irish Sea. What began as a scattered island kingdom has become a maritime power that rivals the Norse and English fleets. Our birlinns are feared in every harbor from Norway to Northumbria.

But how shall we use this dominion? Some captains urge continued raiding: the old Gaelic tradition of plunder and glory. Others see richer prizes in controlling the sea lanes themselves, extracting tolls and establishing trade monopolies.

options.text: Let our raiders strip the coasts bare

modifiers.name: Scourge of the Coasts
modifiers.text: Dalriadic raiders terrorize the coastlines of northern Europe, striking swiftly and vanishing before any response can be organized.

options.text: Control the trade lanes, control the wealth

modifiers.name: Lords of the Sea Lanes
modifiers.text: Dalriada controls the vital sea lanes of the North Atlantic, extracting tolls from every merchant vessel that passes through its waters.

destiny.name: Lord of the Atlantic
destiny.text: The ultimate ambition of the sea-kings: dominion over the Atlantic from the Faroes to the Norwegian coast, making Dalriada the undisputed master of the northern seas. Galley Havens or docks stand in four of its harbours.

conditions.text: A Galley Haven or a port of the dock line (Dock, Dry Dock, Shipyard, Grand Shipyard, Naval Base) stands in at least 4 owned locations

event.title: Lord of the Atlantic
event.text:
From Torshavn to Bergen, from the Hebrides to the Orkneys, the banner of Dalriada flies over every harbor and headland of the North Atlantic. What the Norse achieved through centuries of raiding and settlement, Dalriada has accomplished through the unity of its Gaelic seafaring tradition.

The question now is what form this Atlantic dominion will take. Shall we build an invincible war fleet to defend our vast maritime realm by force of arms? Or shall we consolidate these far-flung territories into a true Atlantic empire, with settlers and administrators binding the islands to the crown?

options.text: Build a fleet to darken the horizon

modifiers.name: The Storm Fleet
modifiers.text: Dalriada maintains the most fearsome naval force in the North Atlantic, a fleet hardened by Atlantic storms and crewed by the finest Gaelic sailors.

options.text: Bind the Atlantic islands into one realm

modifiers.name: Atlantic Empire
modifiers.text: Dalriadic settlers and administrators bind the scattered Atlantic islands into a unified realm, stretching from the Faroes to the Norse coast.

destiny.name: Monastic Revival
destiny.text: Reviving the scholarly tradition of Iona requires foundations. Endow the first two scriptoria of the realm, where monks copy the old books again, and hold and build up Mull, with the abbey of Iona off its shore.

conditions.text: Chose the Flame of Learning destiny
Has a Monastic Scriptorium, a Scriptorium or the printing works that replace it in at least 2 locations
Mull, the island of Iona's abbey, is owned directly and has at least 8 development

event.title: The Scriptoria Reborn
event.text:
Across the islands and glens of Dalriada, the sound of quill on vellum echoes once more. In stone-walled scriptoria warmed by peat fires, monks and scholars copy ancient texts, illuminate manuscripts with the intricate knotwork designs of their ancestors, and compose new works in the Gaelic tongue.

The tradition that gave the world the Book of Kells and the Book of Durrow lives again: not as antiquarian imitation, but as a living scholarly culture that engages with the wider world of European learning.

options.text: Let the light of learning shine anew

destiny.name: Gaelic Letters
destiny.text: Printing transforms Dalriada's monastic tradition into a broader literary culture. Teach one in five of the realm's people to read, and Gaelic books will find readers at home and carry Gaelic thought to a continental audience.

event.title: The Gaelic Press
event.text:
The arrival of the printing press in Dalriada creates a revolution. Where once a single manuscript took months of painstaking labor, now hundreds of copies can be produced in weeks. The bardic schools and monastic scriptoria adapt swiftly, seeing the press not as a threat to their tradition but as its fulfillment.

Gaelic grammars, histories, and poetry pour from the new presses. But debate rages over the direction of this literary flowering. The bardic schools argue for preserving the classical syllabic traditions, while the monastic scholars advocate for broader engagement with the European world.

options.text: Preserve the bardic tradition in print

modifiers.name: Legacy of the File
modifiers.text: The bardic schools preserve and propagate the classical Gaelic literary tradition through the new medium of print, maintaining cultural continuity while reaching wider audiences.

options.text: Spread our learning through monastic networks

modifiers.name: Monastic Commonwealth
modifiers.text: Dalriadic monasteries form a network of learning stretching across northern Europe, sharing texts and scholars in the tradition of Columba's peregrinatio.

destiny.name: Light of the West
destiny.text: The capstone of the Iona tradition: Dalriada becomes a beacon of learning whose scholars and institutions rival any in Europe. Scriptoria work in four of its towns. Derry, the oak grove where Columba founded his first house, is held and built up to twice what it was.

conditions.text: Has a Monastic Scriptorium, a Scriptorium or the printing works that replace it in at least 4 locations
Derry is owned directly and has at least 24 development

event.title: Light of the Western World
event.text:
What Iona was to the Dark Ages, Dalriada has become to the age of the printed book. Its colleges produce scholars whose works are read from Edinburgh to Constantinople. Its printing presses disseminate knowledge in Gaelic, Latin, and the modern tongues. Its monastic libraries (descendants of the scriptoria that preserved civilization during Europe's darkest hours) now house collections that rival the great continental universities.

This intellectual flowering must now find its fullest expression. Shall we channel our scholarly energies toward a great renaissance of Gaelic culture itself? Or shall we open our doors to the wider world, making Dalriada a crossroads of universal knowledge?

options.text: A Gaelic renaissance for the ages

modifiers.name: Gaelic Renaissance
modifiers.text: A conscious flowering of Gaelic culture in all its forms (literature, music, law, and philosophy) asserts the enduring vitality of the Celtic tradition.

options.text: Become the crossroads of all knowledge

modifiers.name: Tradition of Wisdom
modifiers.text: Dalriada becomes a universal center of learning, where scholars of every tradition gather to share knowledge as they once did in the great monastic age.

units.name: Kern Skirmishers
units.text: Light-footed raiding infantry armed with javelins and short swords, the kern are the shock troops of Gaelic warfare: swift, fierce, and utterly fearless.

units.name: Ceithern na Coille
units.text: Woodland warriors who exploit the forests and broken terrain of the western Highlands to devastating effect, ambushing enemies in places where heavy armor is a liability.

units.name: Dalriadic War Galley
units.text: A purpose-built warship combining the shallow draft and speed of the traditional birlinn with mounted cannon, designed for raiding and coastal warfare in the island-studded western seaboard.

buildings.name: Dun
buildings.text: A fortified hilltop stronghold in the ancient Gaelic tradition, commanding the surrounding terrain from its elevated position. The greatest dun of all was Dunadd, seat of the kings of Dalriada.

buildings.name: Cattle Fold
buildings.text: A stone-walled buaile on the hill pasture, where the cattle owed to the chief are gathered, counted and slaughtered. Rent, tribute and the fines of the breitheamh are all reckoned in cows.

where.text: The location's raw material is Livestock

buildings.name: Herring Station
buildings.text: Curing yards on the shore of a sea loch. The catch of the Minch and Loch Fyne is gutted, salted and packed in barrels for the markets of the Baltic and the Lowlands. With the catch cured on the shore, the boats can take the whole run of the herring.

where.text: The location's raw material is Fish

buildings.name: Waulking House
buildings.text: The taigh-luaidh of a township. The web is soaked and beaten by hand on a long board to the rhythm of the waulking songs, then dyed with crotal and heather.

buildings.name: Kelp Kiln
buildings.text: Stone-lined trenches above the tide mark. Tangle cut at low water is dried and burnt to a hard ash, the alkali of the glassmaker and the soap boiler, and a glasshouse beside the kilns uses it on the spot.

buildings.name: Monastic Scriptorium
buildings.text: A workshop within a monastery or religious house dedicated to the copying and illumination of manuscripts, continuing the tradition that produced the Book of Kells.

buildings.name: Clan Hall
buildings.text: The gathering place of the clan chief and his leading men, where disputes are settled by brehon law, alliances are forged over mead, and the affairs of the clan are administered.

buildings.name: Galley Haven
buildings.text: A sheltered coastal anchorage equipped with slipways and repair facilities for the birlinn galley fleet, serving as both a naval base and a hub for coastal trade.

buildings.name: Drove Station
buildings.text: A waystation along the cattle drove roads where herds are rested, watered, and traded, connecting the Highland pastoral economy with lowland and overseas markets.

buildings.name: Birlinn Arsenal
buildings.text: A great naval shipyard and armory dedicated to building and outfitting the Dalriadic war fleet, combining the traditional Gaelic galley-building craft with modern naval technology.

buildings.name: Great Library of Dalriada
buildings.text: A grand repository of learning in the tradition of Iona, housing manuscripts, printed volumes, and scholarly works from across the known world.

list.name: Senchus fer nAlban
list.text: Compiled in the seventh century and surviving in a tenth-century recension, the Senchus fer nAlban ("History of the Men of Scotland") was both genealogy and naval levy register. It prescribed two seven-benched ships from every twenty households of the cenela, an obligation unique among the kingdoms of Britain. Revived as the muster-roll of the reborn sea-kingdom, the Senchus translates Dalriada's coast-and-island geography into permanent fleet manpower under the over-king's call.

list.name: Court of the Breitheamh
list.text: The breitheamh, hereditary jurists of Gaelic Ireland and the Highlands, were trained for as many as twenty years in the customary law of the Senchus Mor. They sat beneath the open sky, arbitrating cattle-claims, eric-payments, and inheritance disputes by precedent rather than royal decree. Their courts ran in parallel to the king's, absorbed grievances that would otherwise have become rebellion, and survived in Gaelic Ireland into the seventeenth century before the Case of Tanistry abolished them in 1608.

list.name: Council of the Isles
list.text: From its first charter under John of Islay to its forfeiture under James IV in 1493, the Comhairle nan Eilean met on Eilean na Comhairle in Loch Finlaggan. Four great chiefs (the Macleans of Duart and Lochbuie, and the Macleods of Harris and Lewis), four lesser thanes, and four kinsmen of Clan Donald deliberated under the lord's presidency, settled disputes between the clans, and committed the lordship's diplomacy and military weight. The council was the most fully developed parliament in Gaelic Britain, and its restoration imposes the same restraints on the crown that its medieval form imposed on the Lord of the Isles.

list.name: Buannacht and Coinnmheadh
list.text: The buannacht, which the English settlers anglicised as bonaght, was the cess by which Gaelic chiefs quartered their gallowglass and household troops on the tuath. The Brehon corpus knew the practice as coinnmheadh; the Anglo-Norman sources rendered it as coyne and livery. Beef, ale, oats, and lodging fed a standing retinue without ever passing through a treasury, and a strong military lord could demand it as often as he had soldiers to enforce it. It was the single most important tax of late-medieval Ireland and the Hebrides, and the chief instrument by which the chiefs kept their armies on the country's back.

list.name: Paruchia of Iona
list.text: The paruchia Columbae was the federation of monasteries founded from Iona under the abbatial succession of Colum Cille (St. Columba, d. 597), reaching across Argyll, the Hebrides, and northern Ireland. It did not take the territorial diocesan form of Roman Christianity; it was a personal-and-monastic network through which scholarship, illuminated manuscripts, and ecclesiastical authority flowed back to the mother-house on Iona. The Annals of Ulster and the Book of Kells were both products of its scriptoria, and its decay into hereditary lay-abbacies (the coarbs and erenaghs) is the cautionary tale of any clerical institution left unmaintained.
